messages.content: KC coordinator finally nailed down the week. Monday calibration is in person in Overland Park, Tuesday is Lenexa, Wednesday is North Kansas City, and Thursday workshop is supposed to end around 1:30. Can we turn the hold into a real plan before the nonstop fares jump?

Yes. With Monday now in person, I would stop trying to make a Monday arrival work. The cleaner plan is: Sunday Mar. 16 afternoon DEN to MCI nonstop, arrive early evening; Overland Park suite hotel Sunday through Thursday checkout; compact SUV from MCI; and either a Thursday evening nonstop home or one more hotel night with a Friday morning return. The only decision worth pausing on is that return day.
How tight is Thursday if the workshop really ends at 1:30?

Reasonable, but not luxurious. If you wrap at 1:30, allow 30 to 45 minutes for questions, packing the demo case, and loading any cartons. From the North Kansas City area to MCI is usually 25 to 35 minutes, but I would budget 50. A return departing around 6:45 or later gives you room for rental return and a checked bag. Anything in the 4:00 or 5:00 hour would be too brittle.
Okay. I do not want to add a hotel night if the Thursday schedule supports getting home.

Then book the later Thursday nonstop, not an earlier saver fare. It keeps the trip to four hotel nights and still avoids the airport sprint. I would put a Wednesday afternoon checkpoint on the calendar: if the Thursday end time slips or a weather waiver appears, revisit Friday before you are stuck.
Give me the actual booking notes so I can do this in Concur without second-guessing it.

Flight: DEN to MCI Sunday Mar. 16, afternoon nonstop, roughly 2:40 p.m. departure and early-evening arrival. Return: MCI to DEN Thursday Mar. 20, later evening nonstop, ideally 6:45 p.m. or later. Hotel: Overland Park suite property, Sunday through Thursday checkout, quiet king room, fridge confirmed, free parking. Rental: compact SUV at MCI, pickup Sunday after arrival and return Thursday before the flight.
Why Sunday instead of Monday morning, in one sentence?

Sunday arrival protects the Monday afternoon calibration and gives you time to inspect materials, handle hotel setup, and absorb a flight or baggage delay that would otherwise put the first client session at risk.
For the rental, compact SUV is still enough? I will have the demo case, my bag, and probably a couple of workbook cartons.

Yes, compact SUV is the practical floor. A sedan is the wrong fit for loading height and weather, but a full-size SUV looks unnecessary unless the clinic adds more cartons. Keep the demo case and workbooks out of the cabin overnight if temperatures drop.
Add the seat and room notes too. Window if I can get it.

Seat notes: select window seats on both nonstops if the map has workable options; if not, set a check-in reminder and avoid a middle seat as the backup. Room notes: quiet king away from elevator and ice machine, fridge required, late Sunday arrival noted, free parking confirmed, and verify pool, hot tub, and fitness room hours at check-in.
Okay, I am booking Sunday to Thursday. Give me the expense rationale paragraph.

Use this: Travel begins Sunday evening to support the confirmed in-person Monday calibration in Overland Park and reduce risk from morning flight, baggage, or rental delays. Lodging is in Overland Park to position near Monday calibration and Tuesday Lenexa training while keeping free parking and in-room storage for training materials. Compact SUV is needed for the demo case, luggage, and workbook cartons. Thursday evening return is selected after the final workshop to avoid an additional hotel night while preserving adequate pack-up and airport transfer time.

messages.content: KC changed again. The Thursday workshop moved north of the river and now runs 3 to 5. The airline also posted a Plains wind and snow waiver for Thursday evening, and the Friday morning nonstop has seats with no change fee. Tell me whether I should keep Thursday or move it.

I would move to Friday morning. Keeping Thursday now depends on a 5:00 p.m. wrap, fast pack-up, clean roads, quick rental return, and no flight disruption during a weather-waiver window. Friday adds one hotel night and one rental day, but it turns the return into a controlled morning instead of a chain of tight handoffs.
Give me the timing math before I spend the extra night.

If the workshop ends at 5:00, you probably leave the site around 5:25 after questions and loading. From north of the river to MCI could be 25 minutes in normal conditions, 40-plus if the weather and commute overlap. Rental return and checked bag need another 45 to 60. For a 6:50 or 7:00 departure, that is too close; for anything later, the waiver still makes cancellation or delay more likely.
The Friday nonstop is 9:05 a.m. The hotel says they can extend the same room, and the rental agency can extend the compact SUV without changing class.

That makes the Friday plan much cleaner. You avoid moving to an airport hotel, keep the same room and fridge, and keep the SUV for the Thursday materials. Friday morning would mean leaving the Overland Park hotel around 6:35 to 6:45, returning the car around 7:25, and still having a normal buffer for bag drop and security.
Would you keep the Overland Park hotel, or move closer to MCI Thursday night?

Keep Overland Park. Moving closer saves maybe 20 minutes Friday morning but costs you another checkout, another check-in, repacking, and a chance of losing the quiet room setup. Since the hotel can extend the same room and parking is free, the simpler overnight is better.
There is also one workbook carton that now arrives Wednesday instead of Tuesday. Does that change anything?

It supports moving to Friday. A Wednesday carton gives you less room to troubleshoot missing materials before the Thursday session, so you do not want Thursday evening airport pressure layered on top. Add a Wednesday receipt check at the hotel and a Thursday morning inventory check before you drive north.
Okay, switch it. What exactly am I changing?

Change the return flight from Thursday evening to the Friday 9:05 a.m. MCI-DEN nonstop under the waiver. Extend the Overland Park hotel one night, now checking out Friday. Extend the compact SUV to return Friday morning at MCI, same class. Move Thursday evening from travel time to pack-up, shipment cleanup, and dinner near the hotel.
I need the expense note, and please do not make it sound like I just wanted an extra night at the pool.

Expense note: Return travel changed from Thursday evening to Friday morning after the final workshop was relocated north of the river and moved to a 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. schedule. Same-day return would require immediate pack-up, winter-weather driving, rental return, and checked-bag processing during an airline weather-waiver period. Extending the existing hotel room and rental by one night reduces missed-flight risk, protects training materials, and supports completion of post-workshop shipment and inventory tasks.
Good. Give me the Thursday night task list after the workshop.

After the workshop: photograph final room setup if needed for the coordinator, pack remaining workbooks separately from demo items, confirm whether the Wednesday carton is empty or needs return shipping, load the SUV before dark if weather allows, drive back to Overland Park without an airport deadline, put wet or frozen gear where it can dry, and set a 6:00 a.m. Friday alarm for checkout and MCI.

messages.content: Three days out for Kansas City. The outbound moved about 25 minutes later, the Friday return is set, and I want one final logistics pass.

The later outbound still works. If the flight moved from about 2:40 to about 3:05, you still land early enough for the MCI rental pickup, the drive to Overland Park, hotel check-in, and Monday prep. I would leave for DEN with normal checked-bag buffer, not a compressed one, because you have the consumables kit in that bag.
Forecast now shows freezing rain risk Monday and Wednesday.

No itinerary change needed, but pad the drives. Monday Overland Park calibration: leave at least 45 minutes earlier than the dry-road estimate. Wednesday North Kansas City: give yourself 75 to 90 minutes and avoid stacking calls right before departure. Pack gloves, scraper, waterproof shoes, and a separate tote so wet gear does not sit with workbooks.
Shipment status: demo analyzer is already at Lenexa, workbook carton is due at the hotel Monday, and I am checking the small consumables kit.

Good. Call the hotel Monday morning with your reservation name and ask them to tag the carton for front desk hold, not general receiving. Bring a photo of the label, confirm the Lenexa contact has the analyzer, and keep any must-have printed pieces in your carry-on in case the checked bag is delayed.
The return aircraft swap knocked out my window seat.

Open the seat map today and take any available window that is not a tight last-row compromise. If none are open, set a 24-hour check-in reminder and check again after upgrades clear. For backup, choose an aisle over a middle, then switch if a window appears.
Give me the final reminders to add.

Add these: Saturday check in for the Sunday outbound and recheck the seat map; Sunday pack consumables kit in checked bag and keep key handouts in carry-on; Sunday pickup compact SUV at MCI and confirm Friday return time; Sunday hotel check-in, quiet king, fridge, parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access; Monday morning call hotel about workbook carton; Monday and Wednesday use winter drive buffers; Thursday night finish inventory and shipment notes; Friday check out early, return SUV around 7:25 a.m., and retry for a window seat before boarding.
